clue.text: Military medic given honour and special attire

blocks.note: military matters are matters of war
DR is the abbreviation for doctor
the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: An army doctor receives a decoration and a special uniform to wear for the ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe is a stock of clothes, especially the costumes kept by a theatre company for performances.

clue.text: Name of socialist couple in network broadcasting originally

indicators.note: originally points to how a word begins, so only its opening letter is used

blocks.note: a web is a network, as in the World Wide Web
the first letter of broadcasting

explanation.surface: Talk of a left-wing pair appearing in a broadcasting network.
explanation.walkthrough: Sidney and Beatrice Webb were the Fabian socialist couple who helped found the London School of Economics.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname shared by Sidney and Beatrice, famous husband-and-wife Fabian reformers and writers.

clue.text: Superb, but not well done?

blocks.note: first meaning: exceptionally fine
second meaning: of meat, lightly cooked and still red inside

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites reading 'not well done' as a criticism of a performance, but it is the cook's term for steak.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means both unusually excellent and, of steak, cooked only briefly so the inside stays pink.

clue.text: One who may find error in a proof?

definitions.text: One who may find error in a proof?

blocks.clueFragment: One who may find error in a proof?
blocks.note: surface reading: a mathematician or logician spotting a flaw in an argument
setter's reading: a printer's proof, checked for typos by someone employed to do so

explanation.walkthrough: A proof is a trial printing of text; the person checking it for mistakes is a proofreader, here shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: A publisher's reader, or proofreader, goes through galley proofs marking printing mistakes before publication.

clue.text: Brunel seen as a diplomatic type?

definitions.note: an example: Isambard Kingdom Brunel built famous bridges

blocks.note: first meaning: the Victorian engineer, literally a builder of bridges such as the Clifton Suspension Bridge
second meaning: someone who reconciles opposing sides

explanation.surface: Was the great engineer really something of a diplomat?
explanation.walkthrough: Isambard Kingdom Brunel was a 19th-century British engineer of railways, ships and bridges.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively, a peacemaker who connects hostile parties is said to build bridges between them.

clue.text: Asked to have breakfast in bed?

indicators.note: in tells us one item sits inside the other, as food rests in a bed

blocks.note: an egg is a typical breakfast
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone requested breakfast to be brought up to them in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The egg goes inside the bed: B-EGG-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Begged is the past tense of beg, to request earnestly, so it matches the verb asked.

clue.text: One in the clan, out of place in a particular group

indicators.note: the word in places one element inside the following phrase
letters out of place are disordered and must be rearranged

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clan member who feels like a misfit within a particular group.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethnical, an old form of ethnic, describes what belongs to a particular race or cultural community.

clue.text: Female relation in army uprising in foreign country

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising lifts the letters so they read from bottom to top
in tells us the preceding letters go inside the country that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
TA is the Territorial Army, the British reserve force
a foreign country to a British setter

explanation.surface: A female relative caught up in a military revolt abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' does double duty in the surface but is used twice in the wordplay: once as letters to keep, once to signal insertion; the TA is Britain's Territorial Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A great-niece is the daughter of one's nephew or niece, a female family member two generations down.

clue.text: You'll be 21 with him, as one who no longer knows the ropes?

definitions.text: one who no longer knows the ropes

blocks.note: first meaning: 21 is the answer at 21-across, seeing double, which is what an exact lookalike makes you think you are doing

blocks.clueFragment: one who no longer knows the ropes
blocks.note: second meaning, cryptically: a bell-ringer who has died no longer handles the bell ropes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Knows the ropes' looks like the idiom for being experienced, but the ropes are literal bell ropes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead ringer is a person who looks exactly like someone else, so seeing them is like seeing double.

clue.text: Is male behind bars for uncivilised behaviour?

indicators.note: behind says the first parts come after what follows, placing them at the end

blocks.note: bars in the plural, read as two of them: BAR and BAR
taken as written
M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Is a man locked up in prison for his savage conduct?
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'bars' supplies two copies of BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Barbarism is savagery or crude conduct of the kind attributed to people lacking civilisation.

clue.text: Rusted man, tutee mostly out of the ordinary?

definitions.text: Rusted man, tutee mostly out of the ordinary?

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all of the word is kept, dropping its last letter
something out of the ordinary is not in its usual form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
tutee without its final letter

explanation.surface: An old rusty fellow who is, for a pupil, rather unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: an older pupil is an unusual tutee.
explanation.definitionFit: A mature student is an adult who enters college or university later than most, an untypical pupil.

clue.text: Animal with desire to break into laugh?

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

blocks.note: ha is the sound of a laugh
a yen is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: Which creature wants to burst out laughing?
explanation.walkthrough: The hyena is known for its laugh-like call, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is a carnivorous African and Asian mammal, a scavenger famous for its cackling cry.

clue.text: Competitor demanding more pounds as he gets better

definitions.text: Competitor demanding more pounds as he gets better

blocks.clueFragment: Competitor demanding more pounds as he gets better
blocks.note: surface reading: a sportsman asking for a pay rise as his form improves
setter's reading: pounds are units of weight, and an improving athlete in this sport hoists ever heavier loads

explanation.walkthrough: Pounds looks like money in a wage demand; it is weight on the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A weightlifter competes by raising heavy barbells, and progress means lifting greater weights.

clue.text: Fan from orient touring province, so enthralled

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the orient word wraps around what follows
enthralled means held captive, so this word is held inside the province

blocks.note: the Orient is the East
NI is Northern Ireland, often called the Province
so and thus are synonyms

explanation.surface: A traveller from the Far East is captivated touring a region.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions nest: the smaller word goes inside the province first, and that result is then wrapped by the orient. Northern Ireland is commonly called the Province in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan is an enthusiast, someone keenly devoted to a team, star or hobby.

clue.text: Poet, who's head and shoulders above others?

definitions.text: who's head and shoulders above others

blocks.note: first meaning: Henry Wadsworth, American author of Hiawatha

blocks.clueFragment: who's head and shoulders above others
blocks.note: second meaning, read literally: a tall chap, a man of great height

explanation.walkthrough: 'Head and shoulders above others' normally means far superior; here it is literal height, splitting the name into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Wadsworth Longfellow was a celebrated nineteenth-century American poet, and a long fellow is a tall man.

clue.text: Opening number doing the business

blocks.note: NO is the abbreviation for number
something that does the business is satisfactory, all right

explanation.surface: An opening song that does its job well.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small recess or opening in a wall or corner of a room.

clue.text: Mistake gives Scottish city only half the quota

indicators.note: only half means the rest of the city name is dropped, keeping its first portion

blocks.note: Aberdeen is a city in north-east Scotland
a ration is a fixed allowance or quota

explanation.surface: A blunder means a Scottish city receives just half its allocation.
explanation.definitionFit: An aberration is a departure from what is normal or right, so a lapse or error.

clue.text: As a woman she can't be matched

definitions.text: As a woman she can't be matched

blocks.clueFragment: As a woman she can't be matched
blocks.note: surface reading: praise for a woman without equal
setter's reading: matched as in married off, so a woman who has never been paired with a husband

explanation.walkthrough: 'Can't be matched' sounds like high praise, but it means unmarried.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional term for an unmarried woman, especially an older one who has never wed.

clue.text: This prig - he is unfit to be a religious leader

indicators.note: unfit suggests something not in proper shape, so the letters must be put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A sanctimonious prude is judged unsuitable to lead a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A high priest is the chief cleric of a religion, as in ancient Judaism, or figuratively the head of a movement.

clue.text: Longing to be a cult hero

blocks.note: taken as written
Che Guevara, the revolutionary whose face became a cult icon

explanation.surface: Yearning to become an idol worshipped by fans.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to yearn for it, so an ache is a strong desire.

clue.text: Girl left to be protected by very good boy

indicators.note: something protected is shielded on both sides, so it sits within the letters that follow

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
A1 means first-rate, with the 1 written as the letter I
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A young woman is looked after by a well-behaved lad.
explanation.definitionFit: Alison is a female first name, so it is a crossword's standard girl.

clue.text: Under the influence? One's beguiled, possibly

indicators.note: possibly hints the letters given could form something else when reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drunk person might find themselves charmed into confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: seeing double is a symptom of drunkenness rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone heavily intoxicated may have blurred vision and perceive two of everything.

clue.text: Rodent climbing round plant

indicators.note: in a down answer climbing means the word goes upward, read from bottom to top

blocks.note: a rat is a rodent
the letter O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A rat scrambles up and around a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Taro is a tropical plant grown for its starchy edible root, used in Pacific and Asian cooking.

clue.text: Dishonourable grass

blocks.note: first meaning: corrupt, crooked, as of a policeman
second meaning: a kind of stiff grass also called bentgrass

explanation.walkthrough: Grass can be British slang for an informer, which fits a crooked surface, but here it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Bent is slang for corrupt or crooked, and also the name of a wiry grass used for lawns.

clue.text: Hand out everyone books in church?

blocks.note: all means everyone
OT is the Old Testament, books read in church

explanation.surface: Distribute hymnals or Bibles to the whole congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or apportion shares among people, which is handing them out.

clue.text: Eve learns to change being subject again

indicators.note: to change the words is to alter their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Eve discovers how to reinvent herself, becoming a different person once more.
explanation.definitionFit: To subject someone again is to bring them back under domination, putting them in bondage a second time.

clue.text: Vulgar rebel about to get boring

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the rebel's name runs backwards

blocks.note: Wat Tyler led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381
dry means dull, boring

explanation.surface: A coarse revolutionary is about to turn tedious.
explanation.definitionFit: Tawdry means showy but cheap and in poor taste, so tasteless or vulgar.

clue.text: Protrude with fat spreading around

indicators.note: spreading around means extending on every side to enclose something

blocks.note: and means with, along with
stout means fat, portly

explanation.surface: A paunch sticks out as fat expands around the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: To protrude is to project beyond a surface, which is what sticking or standing out means.
